{{MedalGold|[[2017 FIBA Asia Cup|2017 Lebanon]]|}} }} '''Mitchell Creek''' (born 27 April 1992) is an Australian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Vancouver Bandits]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]] (CEBL). He began his [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) career in 2010 and played his first eight seasons with the [[Adelaide 36ers]]. After a stint in Germany in 2018, he joined the [[Long Island Nets]] of the [[NBA G League]]. During the 2018–19 season, he had stints in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] and [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. He played for the [[South East Melbourne Phoenix]] between 2019 and 2024. ==Early life and career== Creek was born and raised in [[Horsham, Victoria]].{{cite web |title=Adelaide 36ers Roster |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/36ers/team/players/ |website=nbl.com.au |access-date=23 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110224231930/http://www.nbl.com.au/36ers/team/players/ |archive-date=24 February 2011 |url-status=dead}}{{cite web |title=Mitch Creek |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/teams/36ers/team/players/mitch-creek/ |website=nbl.com.au |access-date=23 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101211172613/http://www.nbl.com.au/teams/36ers/team/players/mitch-creek/ |archive-date=11 December 2010 |quote=Hometown is Horsham in rural Victoria. |url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nbl/story/_/id/25351109/australian-mitch-creek-thriving-new-york-long-island-nets|title=Mitch Creek is thriving in his NY moment|work=ESPN.com.au|date=23 November 2018|access-date=4 December 2018}} He attended St Brigid's College, where he earned induction into the school's hall of fame.{{cite web|last=Cavalieri|first=Peppe|url=http://www.mailtimes.com.au/story/3636090/st-brigids-college-welcomes-hall-of-fame-inductees-photos/|title=St Brigid's College welcomes Hall of Fame inductees on New Year's Day|work=MailTimes.com.au|date=5 January 2016|access-date=2 May 2016}} He grew up playing for the Horsham Hornets.{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsportspulse.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&client=1-7930-99139-113860-12880305&pID=191474542 |title=Player statistics for Mitch Creek – Big V |work=FoxSportsPulse.com |access-date=2 May 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160506224105/http://www.foxsportspulse.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&client=1-7930-99139-113860-12880305&pID=191474542 |archive-date=6 May 2016 }} In 2009, Creek played a leading role in Victoria Country's campaign at the Under-18 National Championships, trained with the Australian under-19 squad, and earned a place at the prestigious Nike All-Asia Camp in [[Beijing]], China. He also joined the [[Australian Institute of Sport]] (AIS) in [[Canberra]].{{cite web|last=Ward|first=Roy|url=http://www.mailtimes.com.au/story/967763/mitch-creek-scores-ais-chance/|title=Mitch Creek scores AIS chance|work=MailTimes.com.au|date=26 June 2009|access-date=2 May 2016}} He played for the [[BA Centre of Excellence|AIS men's team]] in the [[South East Australian Basketball League]] (SEABL), recording one game in 2009 and 14 games in 2010.{{cite web|url=http://websites.sportstg.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=194499665&client=1-3363-150604-148539-4362809 |title=Player statistics for Mitch Creek – SEABL |work=SportsTG.com |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181204040522/http://websites.sportstg.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=194499665&client=1-3363-150604-148539-4362809 |archive-date=4 December 2018}} In 2010, Creek helped Victoria Country win the gold medal at the Under-20 National Championships and helped the Australian under-19 team win its first gold medal at the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]] in [[Mannheim]], Germany. Creek was subsequently crowned the tournament's most valuable player after averaging 17 points per game and finishing second in efficiency on plus 20.{{cite web|last=Ward|first=Roy|url=http://www.mailtimes.com.au/story/971299/horsham-basketballer-on-top-of-the-world/|title=Horsham basketballer on top of the world|work=MailTimes.com.au|date=11 April 2010|access-date=2 May 2016}}{{cite web|last=Ward|first=Roy|url=http://www.mailtimes.com.au/story/972669/mitch-creek-to-play-for-hornets/|title=Mitch Creek to play for Hornets|work=MailTimes.com.au|date=8 July 2010|access-date=2 May 2016}} In 2011, Creek helped Victoria Country win back-to-back gold medals at the Under-20 National Championships. He subsequently won the Bob Staunton Award for tournament MVP after averaging 19 points, 7.6 rebounds and 3 assists per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/36ers/news/news/article/2011/march/36ers-shine-at-nationals/|title=36ers Shine at Nationals|work=NBL.com.au|date=1 March 2011|access-date=1 March 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110628183025/http://www.nbl.com.au/36ers/news/news/article/2011/march/36ers-shine-at-nationals/|archive-date=28 June 2011|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===Adelaide 36ers (2010–2018)=== Creek joined the [[Adelaide 36ers]] for the [[2010–11 NBL season]]. He made his NBL debut on 3 December 2010, recording seven points and three steals in 21 minutes off the bench in a 92–79 win over the [[Townsville Crocodiles]].{{cite web|last=Rogers|first=Leigh|url=http://www.mailtimes.com.au/story/974416/creek-debuts-in-nbl/|title=Creek debuts in NBL|work=MailTimes.com.au|date=5 December 2010|access-date=2 May 2016}} In 20 games as a rookie, Creek averaged 5.8 points and 2.4 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=http://websites.sportstg.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=191868021&client=0-189-88237-327335-19755570 |title=Player statistics for Mitch Creek – NBL |work=SportsTG.com |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181204042649/http://websites.sportstg.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=191868021&client=0-189-88237-327335-19755570 |archive-date=4 December 2018}} He remained in Adelaide following his rookie season and played for the [[South Adelaide Panthers (basketball)|South Adelaide Panthers]] of the [[Premier League (Australia)|Central ABL]].{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsportspulse.com/assoc_page.cgi?c=1-3656-0-0-0&sID=39560&news_task=DETAIL&articleID=15277426|title=South Adelaide Signs 36er Star Mitch Creek|work=FoxSportsPulse.com|date=31 March 2011|access-date=2 May 2016}} In [[2011–12 NBL season|2011–12]], Creek appeared in all 28 games for the 36ers, averaging 5.4 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game. He again played in the Central ABL during the 2012 off-season, appearing in five games for the Woodville Warriors. Creek's [[2012–13 NBL season|2012–13 season]] was cut short after rupturing his [[Achilles tendon]] on 15 December against the Crocodiles in Adelaide.{{cite web|last=Nagy|first=Boti|url=http://www.adelaidenow.com.au/sport/basketball/nbl-confident-of-an-aerial-threat-in-slam-dunk-contest/story-fndekpx4-1226538687825|title=NBL confident of an aerial threat in Slam Dunk Contest|work=AdelaideNow.com.au|date=17 December 2012|access-date=2 May 2016}}{{cite web|last=McArdle|first=Jordan|url=https://www.mailtimes.com.au/story/1189062/former-horsham-basketballer-mitch-creek-out-for-season/|title=Former Horsham basketballer Mitch Creek out for season|work=MailTimes.com.au|date=17 December 2012|access-date=4 December 2018}}{{cite web|last=McArdle|first=Jordan|url=https://www.mailtimes.com.au/story/1291501/adelaide-36er-mitch-creek-recovering-well-from-achilles-injury/|title=Adelaide 36er Mitch Creek recovering well from achilles injury|work=MailTimes.com.au|date=11 February 2013|access-date=4 December 2018}} In 12 games, he averaged 5.8 points and 2.6 rebounds per game. He returned to action in [[2013–14 NBL season|2013–14]],{{cite web|url=http://www.adelaide36ers.com/article/id/rpbqh7nz2krj1q82d3ssqcn3h|title=Sixers and Lightning re-sign Creek and Mansfield|work=Adelaide36ers.com|date=24 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019194010/http://www.adelaide36ers.com/article/id/rpbqh7nz2krj1q82d3ssqcn3h|archive-date=19 October 2013|url-status=dead}} helping the 36ers reach the NBL Grand Final, where they lost to the [[Perth Wildcats]] in three games. In 33 games, Creek averaged 7.7 points, 3.8 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game. During the 2014 off-season, Creek played in the [[South East Australian Basketball League|SEABL]] for the [[Nunawading Spectres]].{{cite web|url=http://www.seabl.com.au/index.php?id=257&tx_ttnews%5Btt_news%5D=9474&cHash=7372c90ade |title=NUNAWADING LAND NBL RISING STAR MITCH CREEK |work=SEABL.com.au |date=16 March 2014 |access-date=2 May 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20170326061631/http://seabl.com.au/index.php?id=257&tx_ttnews%5Btt_news%5D=9474&cHash=7372c90ade |archive-date=26 March 2017 }} Creek had a career-best season in [[2014–15 NBL season|2014–15]],{{cite web|url=http://www.adelaide36ers.com/article/id/1xrafa5zllf891p6m0bsf01hcd|title=Mitch Creek Signs New Contract To Remain A 36er|work=Adelaide36ers.com|date=14 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514112359/http://www.adelaide36ers.com/article/id/1xrafa5zllf891p6m0bsf01hcd|archive-date=14 May 2014|url-status=dead}} averaging 11.2 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 26 games. During the 2015 off-season, he played for the Woodville Warriors.{{cite web|url=http://websites.sportstg.com/nf/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=202139542&client=1-3656-44094-216804-22177656&ocompID=347153 |title=Player statistics for Mitch Creek – Premier League |work=SportsTG.com |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181204044639/http://websites.sportstg.com/nf/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=202139542&client=1-3656-44094-216804-22177656&ocompID=347153 |archive-date=4 December 2018}} In [[2015–16 NBL season|2015–16]], Creek averaged 9.9 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.1 steals in 26 games for the 36ers. During the 2016 off-season, Creek helped the [[Southern Tigers]] of the [[Premier League (Australia)|South Australian Premier League]] win the [[List of NBL1 Central champions|championship]].{{cite web|url=http://websites.sportstg.com/assoc_page.cgi?client=1-3656-0-0-0&sID=39560&&news_task=DETAIL&articleID=47623401|title=Southern Tigers crowned champions after a superb season|work=SportsTG.com|access-date=4 December 2018|quote=After being named captain for the Adelaide 36ers for the upcoming season, it will be interesting to see if he can continue his dominance.}} web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/randle-leads-sixers-second-spot-ladder/|title=RANDLE LEADS SIXERS TO SECOND SPOT ON LADDER|work=NBL.com.au|date=10 December 2016|access-date=10 December help the 36ers win the minor premiership with a 17–11 record. In 21 games, he averaged 12.1 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.0 steals per game. Despite suffering a broken hand following the 2016–17 season,{{cite web|last=Nagy|first=Boti|url=http://www.adelaidenow.com.au/sport/basketball/greece-the-word-for-adelaide-36ers-swingman-nathan-sobey-while-injured-mitch-creek-misses-nba-window/news-story/59892b494d8b8cbb99330e9e199a4b70|title=Greece the word for Adelaide 36ers swingman Nathan Sobey, while injured Mitch Creek misses NBA window|work=AdelaideNow.com.au|date=2 March 2017|access-date=3 March 2017}} Creek was invited to participate in a free agent mini-camp run by the [[Utah Jazz]] before joining the Jazz's Summer League team.{{cite web|last=Santamaria|first=Liam|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/sobey-hodgson-creek-chase-nba-dream/|title=SOBEY, CREEK AND HODGSON CHASE NBA DREAMS|work=NBL.com.au|date=2 June 2017|access-date=2 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170606004337/http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/sobey-hodgson-creek-chase-nba-dream/|archive-date=6 June 2017|url-status=dead}} In [[2017–18 NBL season|2017–18]], despite missing three weeks with a hamstring injury,{{cite web|url=http://nbl.com.au/news/article/38814-adelaide-star-creek-sidelined-for-extended-period|title=Adelaide star Creek sidelined for extended period|work=NBL.com.au|date=12 December 2017|access-date=12 December 2017}} Creek was named the NBL Fans MVP and earned [[All-NBL Team|All-NBL Second Team]] honours.{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/40457-bryce-cotton-crowned-nbl-mvp-for-201718|title=Bryce Cotton crowned NBL MVP for 2017/18|work=NBL.com.au|date=27 February 2018|access-date=27 February 2018}} Creek helped the 36ers reach the 2018 NBL Grand Final series, where they were defeated 3–2 by Melbourne United. He averaged 14.8 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 2.6 assists in what was a career-best season.{{cite web|last=Uluc|first=Olgun|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/mitch-creek-will-exercise-euroout-clause-wont-return-to-adelaide-36ers-for-201819-nbl-season-sources/news-story/8b16c0012a8fe700a1e7d1849a523104|title=Mitch Creek will exercise Euro-out clause, won't return to Adelaide 36ers for 2018-19 NBL season – sources|work=FoxSports.com.au|date=5 June 2018|access-date=5 June 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/42298-creek-parts-ways-with-sixers-to-chase-nba-dream|title=Creek Parts Ways with Sixers to Chase NBA Dream|work=NBL.com.au|date=5 June 2018|access-date=5 June 2018}} ===Europe, NBA G League and NBA (2018–2019)=== Creek finished the 2017–18 German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] season with [[BG Göttingen]].{{cite web|last=Santamaria|first=Liam|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/41325-creek-signs-short-term-contract-with-german-team|title=Creek Signs Short-Term Contract with German Team|work=NBL.com.au|date=2 April 2018|access-date=2 April 2018}} In seven games, he averaged 11.9 points, 2.7 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game.
